mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point or greater increase in the unemployment rate over the prior 3 months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where UNRATE rises > 0.5pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2% or greater quarterly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations for consumer-sensitive sectors and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where GDPC1 declines > 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 4.5% or higher federal funds rate combined with a 2% or greater monthly decline in industrial production signals a restrictive monetary regime, which reduces capital expenditure and growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and INDPRO falls > 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3 percentage point or greater increase in the unemployment rate over the prior 6 months combined with a 1% or greater decline in average hourly earnings (PAYEMS) signals a deteriorating labor cost environment, which reduces profit margins and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 6 months AND PAYEMS falls > 1% year-over-year
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp and PAYEMS falls > 1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 5% or greater monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals strengthening household demand, which boosts earnings expectations for consumer-sensitive sectors and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where GDPC1 rises > 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3% or greater monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals improving manufacturing activity and capacity utilization, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where INDPRO rises > 3% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 0.4 percentage point or greater decrease in the unemployment rate over the prior 6 months combined with a 1.5% or greater increase in average hourly earnings (PAYEMS) signals a tightening labor market with rising wage pressure, which compresses profit margins and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls > 0.4pp in 6 months AND PAYEMS rises > 1.5% year-over-year
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where UNRATE falls > 0.4pp and PAYEMS rises > 1.5% (t-test p > 0.05).
